question.text: What common theme emerges from the PMLA enforcement cases studied in the NISM IFSCA-01 curriculum?

answer.text: Reporting entities face significant penalties for failing to implement effective AML/CFT systems including KYC verification, ongoing due diligence, record maintenance, and suspicious transaction reporting
PMLA enforcement actions are limited to warnings and no monetary penalties are ever imposed
Only large multinational banks are subject to PMLA enforcement, while smaller entities are exempt
PMLA enforcement cases are purely theoretical and have never resulted in actual penalties

explanation.text: The Logic: Across the cases discussed — Bybit (Rs 9.27 crore penalty), Paytm (multiple charges), Prowess (authorization cancelled), and Way2Wealth (compliance deficiencies) — the recurring theme is that non-compliance with AML/CFT expectations (KYC, ongoing CDD, transaction monitoring, record-keeping, and suspicious transaction reporting) leads to real penalties and even cancellation of authorisations for reporting entities. The Trap: Options B, C, and D are incorrect. Option B wrongly claims only warnings are issued; substantial monetary penalties have been imposed. Option C wrongly suggests size-based exemption — entities of all sizes face enforcement. Option D wrongly treats PMLA enforcement as theoretical despite documented penalties. Note: These case studies are tested in NISM IFSCA-01 to reinforce that AML compliance is mandatory and carries real consequences.
